body.estimand_functional: \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}=\operatorname{hull}\{\vartheta\in\Theta:\inf_{c\in\mathcal G_c}\Delta_n(c,\vartheta)\le\Gamma_n(\delta_n)\}\). The proved minimax converse is \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) over the full declared strength shell; the matching profile upper comparison \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\asymp r_n\) remains proposed only on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\).

sampling_model.design: Independent random design with \(X_i\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) and an unknown law-specific cutoff \(c_P\in[1/4,3/4]\).
sampling_model.units: The observations are \(O_i=(X_i,D_i,Y_i)\), for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with binary treatment and outcome.
sampling_model.treatment: The instrument is \(Z_i=\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge c_P\}\), and monotone response types imply \(D_i=D_i(Z_i)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The compliance jump lies in \([\kappa_n,2\kappa_n]\). The main class imposes no outcome-variance, residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor; every binary treatment--outcome association compatible with the observable margins and causal model is allowed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Separate one-sided radius-\(M\), order-\(s\) H\"older extensions are imposed only on the observable treatment and outcome margins. Association is a free binwise Fr\'echet coordinate. A four-cell method-of-types threshold gives finite-sample calibration on certified grids, and the rule returns the full parameter space on each enumerated fallback branch.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Their Theorem 1 establishes honesty of the bias-aware Anderson--Rubin confidence set at a known cutoff.
Their weak-identification-robust fuzzy-RD procedure inverts a reduced-form test at a fixed known cutoff.
Their unknown-threshold result transfers the minimax rate for estimating a sharp-RD discontinuity location from a convolution white-noise model.
Their moderate-break analysis derives a Gaussian-process limit experiment and a nearly weighted-average-power maximizing test.
Their Theorem 1 gives uniformly asymptotically valid conditional tests with a functional nuisance parameter.
Their Theorem 1 shows that risk functions attainable in the weak-GMM Gaussian-process experiment bound finite-sample asymptotic risk.
Their Theorem 3.1 characterizes optimal one-sided confidence intervals through an ordered modulus over convex fixed-index regression classes.
Their sharp testable implications for fuzzy-RD validity are inequalities in the joint outcome--treatment distribution at the cutoff.
Their LoTTA model propagates posterior uncertainty about an unknown cutoff into fuzzy-RD effect estimation.
Their main unknown-discontinuity theory treats testing and estimation in sharp RD, with fuzzy RD discussed separately.

body.tldr: For fuzzy regression discontinuity with a weak compliance jump and unknown cutoff, cutoff recovery and causal-effect informativeness are distinct. The moving-cutoff continuum now gives the explicit finite-sample lower value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), and a causal-valid fixed-cutoff bump continuum gives the nonparametric term \(\min\{1,\rho_n/\kappa_n\}\). Together they prove the all-strength converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) under the unchanged binary H\"older-margin class, while the existing upper bound gives the exact flat-face limit \(2(1-\alpha)\). Finite-grid four-cell calibration remains valid for every compatible treatment--outcome association, including singular cells. The open kernel is the \(s=1\) critical decision value and a continuum-honest, support-wide profile interval with controlled stochastic, discretization, certificate, and fallback remainders; no profile upper rate or finite-positive critical value is claimed as proved.

project_justification.gap: Known-cutoff weak-fuzzy inference, sharp-RD unknown-cutoff rates, generic weak-identification decision theory, and Bayesian propagation of cutoff uncertainty have been developed separately. None supplies an all-strength minimax converse together with an attaining honest connected interval when the cutoff and fuzzy denominator weaken jointly; the converse is now proved here, whereas attainment remains open.
project_justification.niche: The preserved binary uniform-design class makes two complementary causal lifts explicit while leaving the observable treatment--outcome association unrestricted. A moving-cutoff continuum measures slope-location ambiguity and a fixed-cutoff compact bump measures ordinary nonparametric jump difficulty, producing a nonregular location/effect problem that is neither a fixed-boundary modulus problem nor a parametric unknown-break problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the lower frontier by combining the integrated moving-cutoff value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\) with a same-class fixed-cutoff bump bound, yielding \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\) for every declared strength. It also defines a support-wide four-cell profile and coarsened exact calibration that leave association free. The matching upper frontier, the complete critical experiment, and a total attaining interval remain the stated unresolved contribution.

body.related_work: Hahn, Todd, and van der Klaauw (2001) supply the local Wald identification argument. Feir, Lemieux, and Marmer (2016) and Noack and Rothe (2024, Theorem 1) give weak-identification-robust inference at a fixed known cutoff; they do not address translated cutoff/effect ambiguity. The new fixed-cutoff bump continuum recovers the usual nonparametric weak-denominator difficulty inside the present binary class, while the moving-cutoff continuum adds the distinct \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) difficulty and its explicit integrated value \(G_\alpha\). Porter and Yu (2015, Sections 3--5) and Tuvaandorj (2020, Sections 3--4) study unknown-location behavior predominantly in sharp designs, without this weak causal ratio or connected honest-length criterion. Elliott and M\"uller (2014, Sections 2.1--2.3) motivate process experiments for moderate unknown breaks, but do not solve the present H\"older-margin decision problem. Andrews and Mikusheva (2016, Theorem 1) and Andrews and Mikusheva (2022, Theorem 1 and Section 4) inform nuisance calibration and weak-decision analysis; Armstrong and Koles{\'a}r (2018, Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.4) connect testing power to expected length over convex fixed-index classes. None of these results proves the still-open support-wide profile upper bound over the translated nonconvex union. Arai, Hsu, Kitagawa, Mourifi{\'e}, and Wan (2022, Section 2) motivate retaining the full joint outcome--treatment law. Kowalska, van de Wiel, and van der Pas (2025 version, Sections 3 and 6) propagate unknown-cutoff uncertainty in a Bayesian model without uniform frequentist honesty or minimax length.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A product of the two marginal Bernoulli likelihoods is not the likelihood of the observed pair when association is unrestricted. The finite-grid calibration therefore uses the complete binned four-cell vector and a method-of-types threshold that remains valid on singular cell faces. Its dimension cost \(\zeta_n\) need not be negligible on every sequence satisfying cutoff recovery; the stated upper-rate comparison is therefore confined to \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\), while a sharper association-robust calibration for the remainder of \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{recovered}}\) stays open. Separately, an untruncated second moment of a translated-cutoff mixture does not determine a critical constant; boundary truncation, mixture renormalization, the signed effect label, and second-order centering must remain in the experiment.
body.honest_scope: The model has no outcome-variance, null-residual-variance, covariance-eigenvalue, or joint-cell positivity floor, and the new lower bound adds none. The proved results now include the moving-cutoff causal lift and its Kullback--Leibler bound, the explicit integrated lower value \(G_\alpha(\tau_n)\), the exact flat-face limit, the fixed-cutoff compact-bump causal lift and its \(n(\kappa_n|u|)^{2+1/s}\) divergence bound, and the all-strength minimax converse \(L_n^\star(\kappa_n)\gtrsim r_n\). Exact finite-grid four-cell calibration and population false-split separation are also proved, uniformly over permitted binary treatment--outcome associations. These facts do not establish continuum honesty, an upper expected-length rate, or attainment by \(I_n^{\mathrm{prof}}\). The finite-positive decision values, full-model least favorability, continuum discretization, localized stochastic profile bound, and negligible fallback risk remain open. A matching upper comparison is still only a proposed goal on \(\mathfrak R_{\mathrm{cert}}\). No smoothness of joint cells, conditional independence for the full class, association separation, cross-side derivative matching, oracle cutoff, or known association nuisance is imposed.
